record.context_brief: Broadest algebraic setting for duality and MacWilliams relations
record.original_question: Determine the largest class of algebraic structures A for which one can define a duality theory for codes together with MacWilliams relations.

evidence.quote: Open Question 4.4. Find the largest class of algebraic structures A for which a duality and MacWilliams relations hold.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let A denote a finite algebraic structure (for example, a finite group, ring, module, or more general finite algebraic object) and, for each positive integer n, equip A^n with a notion of "code" (a distinguished family of substructures C ⊆ A^n) and a notion of "dual code" C^⊥ ⊆ A^n. Assume each code C carries a Hamming weight enumerator W_C(x,y) = Σ_{c∈C} x^{n−wt(c)} y^{wt(c)}, where wt(c) is the number of nonzero coordinates of c. One says that a "duality theory with MacWilliams relations" exists for A if there is an involutive duality operation C ↦ C^⊥ on codes in A^n (for every n) together with an identity of the form
   W_{C^⊥}(x,y) = (1/|C|) · W_C(x + (q−1)y, x − y)
or, more generally, W_{C^⊥}(x,y) = (1/|C|) · W_C(T(x,y)) for some fixed linear transformation T depending only on A, that holds for every code C ⊆ A^n and every n ≥ 1.

It is classically known that such a duality theory with MacWilliams relations exists when A is a finite field, a finite abelian group (with additive codes), or a finite Frobenius ring (with left/right linear codes).

Problem. Determine the largest class of finite algebraic structures A for which a duality theory together with MacWilliams relations (in the sense above) can be defined.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of finding the largest class of algebraic structures admitting a MacWilliams duality remains open. Frobenius rings are currently the broadest well-established class for which such a duality theory works for linear codes, and finite abelian groups work for additive codes. Negative results (e.g., no MacWilliams duality holds in general for nonabelian groups) have ruled out certain extensions, but no complete characterization of the maximal class is known.

status_evidence.title: No MacWilliams duality for codes over nonabelian groups
status_evidence.snippet: There does not exist a nonabelian group G with a duality theory on the subgroups of G^n for all n.
status_evidence.claim: Extension of MacWilliams duality to nonabelian groups in full generality is impossible, showing the boundary problem is still being explored.

status_evidence.title: MacWilliams extension theorems and the local–global property for codes over Frobenius rings
status_evidence.snippet: MacWilliams identities hold for linear codes over a finite Frobenius ring.
status_evidence.claim: Frobenius rings are the currently established broad class supporting MacWilliams identities for linear codes.

status_evidence.title: Weights on finite fields and failures of the MacWilliams identities
status_evidence.snippet: Studies under which generalized weights MacWilliams-type identities can or cannot hold.
status_evidence.claim: Active recent research continues to probe the boundary of where MacWilliams-style identities exist.
